preamble: Secondary palatalization of the voiced velar stop [ɡ] to [ɡʲ] before front vowels. In Russian, between the 12th and 14th centuries the allophone of /i/ after velars changed from [ɨ] to [i] with subsequent palatalization of the velar (Old Russian гыбкыи [ɡɨpkɨj] > гибкий [ɡʲipkʲij]). In Japanese, only the palatalized variant of a consonant occurs before /i/, so /ɡi/ is [ɡʲi]. In Lithuanian, consonants before front vowels are palatalized (gėlė [ɡʲeːˈlʲeː], gilus [ɡʲɪˈlʊs]).

examples.note: After velars [ɨ] became [i] between the 12th and 14th centuries, and the velar was then palatalized; spelling ги- replaced гы-.
Palatalized and plain consonants contrast before back vowels but only the palatalized version occurs before /i/.
Consonants preceding the front vowels /ɪ, iː, ɛ, æː, eː/ are palatalized.

sources: Wikipedia. History of the Russian language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Russian_language
